# Svelte Commerce

> Svelte Commerce is a production-ready open-source headless ecommerce storefront built with
> SvelteKit and TypeScript. It connects to commerce backends through APIs, letting developers build
> fast, SEO-friendly storefronts independently of their ecommerce backend — and customize the
> storefront by prompting, because the commerce layer sits behind a single service import.

- Entity: Svelte Commerce
- Type: Open-source software
- Category: Headless ecommerce storefront
- Framework: SvelteKit 2 (Svelte 5)
- Language: TypeScript
- Styling: Tailwind CSS, shadcn components
- Architecture: Headless, backend-agnostic via interchangeable connector packages
- License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/itswadesh/svelte-commerce
- Website: https://svelte-commerce.pages.dev

## What it does

Svelte Commerce renders the shopper-facing storefront — catalogue, search, product detail, cart,
checkout, orders and account — and reads all commerce data from an existing backend over that
platform's API. It does not store products, process payments or provide an admin; those remain
with the backend.

## How backends are swapped

Every backend is a connector package implementing one shared service interface. Application code
imports commerce services only from `$lib/core/services` and never names a backend, so changing
platform is a single export change in `kitcommerce.config.ts` plus the matching package install.

## Supported backends

26 connectors. Coverage is the number of storefront services wired to a real endpoint.

Env wiring ships with the repo: Vendure (39/43), Litekart (39/43), Medusa (31/43), Saleor (28/43).

Connector published, env branch added by the user: Broadleaf (28/43), Shopware (28/43),
Virto Commerce (28/43), WooCommerce (27/43), Magento (26/43), Spree (26/43), X-Cart (26/43),
EverShop (25/43), Spryker (25/43), nopCommerce (24/43), PrestaShop (24/43), Sylius (24/43),
Swell (23/43), Bagisto (22/43), commercetools (21/43), OroCommerce (21/43), Sharetribe (21/43),
CS-Cart (20/43), Shuup (19/43), Shopify (16/27), Django Oscar (15/43), OpenCart (9/43).

## Features

- Server-side rendering with client-side navigation after first paint
- Installable PWA
- Product catalogue, category and collection pages
- Search with faceted filtering
- Product detail with variants and options
- Cart, coupons and checkout (address, shipping, payment method, success)
- Authentication: email and OTP login, signup, password reset
- Account: orders, order detail, addresses, profile, wishlist
- Switchable themes resolved at runtime
- SEO: dynamic metadata, canonical URLs, product structured data, sitemap, robots
- Typed end to end; `npm run check` verifies the whole app

## Maturity

The storefront runs in production on Litekart. Each connector is written against its platform's
authoritative API specification — OpenAPI document, GraphQL schema or published contract — and
type-checks against it, but the connectors have not all been verified against live production
stores. Per-platform gaps and open questions are published in the capability matrix.
